newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission delays ruling on Austria's maize ban.
newsitem.headline: Commission delays ruling on Austria's maize ban.

text.p: The European Commission delayed on Wednesday a decision on whether to allow Austria to keep its import ban on genetically modified maize, a spokesman said.
"The Commission has not been able to finalise its work as foreseen," spokesman Peter Jorgensen told a news conference, saying that a decision was unlikely before July.
He added that none of the scientific evidence supplied by Vienna appeared to vindicate Austria's decision to act against the Commission's decision of last December to clear the maize for EU sale.

The Commission has sent Austria's arguments to the three EU scientific committees responsible for assessing the original authorisation and will draft its response on the basis of their findings, Jorgensen said.
A Commission proposal will then go before EU national governments, who will have a month or so to respond, taking a final decision on the validity of the ban into July, he added.

Genetically modified organisms (GMOs) such as the maize sold by newly created Swiss company Novartis and soybeans sold by U.S. company Monsanto, have stirred up a political storm over food policy in the Europe Union.

The Commission is due next week to lay out its view of the issues arising from the increased use of GMOs, hoping to point a way out of the current confusion surrounding the authorisation, labelling and use of such food technologies.
